title: Mission 05: The Decommission
story: The audit cleared. Now the dangerous part: decommissioning. The old project space is full of junk that must go and evidence that must STAY. rm has no undo and no recycle bin - in this job, precision is the skill. One careless wildcard and you are explaining yourself to Legal.

badge.name: The Decommission: Surgical
badge.desc: Mastered rm by deleting exactly what had to go and nothing that had to stay.

tasks.brief: Read BRIEFING5.txt in your department directory. Warm up: remove the single scratch file decommission/scratch.tmp.
Remove EVERY expired certificate (expired_*.cert) from decommission/ in one wildcard sweep. The active certificates (active_*.cert) are evidence: they must all survive.

checks.fail: Expired certificates still remain in decommission/.
Active certificates were deleted. That wildcard was too greedy - Legal has been notified.

tasks.brief: The old_builds directory goes entirely - the folder AND everything in it. Plain rm refuses a directory; it takes one more option.

checks.fail: decommission/old_builds still exists (directories need rm's recursive option).

tasks.brief: Something hidden is squatting in decommission/: a dotfile of cache junk. Find it (you learned how in Mission 02) and remove it.

checks.fail: The hidden cache junk file is still in decommission/ (list with hidden entries shown, then remove it).

tasks.brief: Empty the cache/ directory: every file inside goes, but the cache/ directory ITSELF stays (the nightly job recreates its contents and needs the folder).

checks.fail: cache/ itself was deleted. The nightly job needs the directory - only its CONTENTS go.
cache/ still has contents. Everything inside it goes.
The keep/ evidence was touched. Nothing in keep/ was ever to be deleted or modified.
Even the briefing is gone. Deletion discipline means knowing where the blast radius ends.

tasks.brief: BONUS: a corrupted export created a file literally named -rf inside decommission/. rm treats it as an option, not a filename. Two idioms get past that; use either and remove it.

checks.fail: The file named -rf still exists (hint: a -- end-of-options marker, or a ./ path prefix).
